SWPROJ_REQ_009a: As a field technician using the home/map screen, I want the map to be the dominant visual element so that I can locate my next job site without navigating through additional screens. On application launch, the home screen shall display an interactive map component that occupies at least 70% (assumed) of the visible viewport height, excluding the status/header bar, consistent with the "Field App Design System v2.1" (assumed) style guide. Acceptance criteria: (1) map viewport coverage is measured and confirmed to be ≥70% on reference devices with screen widths of 360px and 414px (assumed); (2) no modal, banner, or panel shall reduce map visibility below this threshold by default; (3) QA verifies compliance via automated UI layout snapshot testing.

SWPROJ_REQ_009b: As a field technician, I want a minimal primary navigation menu so that I can reach any core feature (map, job list, profile, settings) in no more than 2 taps from the home screen, reducing time spent searching for functions. The home screen's primary navigation shall contain no more than 3 top-level items (assumed: Map, Jobs, Profile), each leading directly to its destination screen without intermediate menus. Acceptance criteria: (1) primary navigation item count is verified to be ≤3 via UI inspection; (2) all core features listed in the information architecture are reachable within 2 taps/clicks from the home screen, validated through usability testing with at least 5 field technician users (assumed); (3) average task completion time to reach any core feature is ≤5 seconds (assumed) as measured in usability testing.
notes: N: prescribes 70% map layout & 3-item nav; S: bundles map layout + nav/usability testing

**MICROCARE_REQ_002-A: Client and Partner ID Resolution for Voucher Issuance**

As a Voucher Issuance System, I need to resolve a unique Client ID and a unique Partner ID at the moment a voucher is created, so that each voucher slip can be traced to both parties for redemption and settlement.

- Client ID: a pre-existing 10-character alphanumeric identifier (assumed) already assigned to the client during registration.
- Partner ID: a pre-existing 10-character alphanumeric identifier (assumed) already assigned to the partner during onboarding.

Acceptance Criteria:
1. Given a voucher is being issued for a registered client and an active partner, When the issuance process runs, Then the system retrieves and attaches the existing Client ID and Partner ID to the voucher record.
2. Given a voucher is issued without an assigned partner (generic/unassigned voucher), When the issuance process runs, Then the system attaches a reserved placeholder Partner ID value of "UNASSIGNED00" (assumed) instead of failing.
3. Given a Client ID cannot be found for the requesting client, When the issuance process runs, Then the system rejects voucher creation and returns an error code "ERR_CLIENT_ID_NOT_FOUND" (assumed).

---

**MICROCARE_REQ_002-B: Barcode Encoding of Client and Partner IDs**

As a Voucher Issuance System, I need to generate two separate Code 128 barcodes (assumed symbology) for each voucher slip — one encoding the Client ID and one encoding the Partner ID — so that each party can be scanned and identified independently during redemption and settlement.

Acceptance Criteria:
1. Given a voucher with a resolved Client ID and Partner ID, When the barcodes are generated, Then two distinct Code 128 barcodes are produced: one encoding only the Client ID string and one encoding only the Partner ID string.
2. Given a voucher with an unassigned Partner ID ("UNASSIGNED00"), When the barcodes are generated, Then the Partner barcode still encodes this placeholder value rather than being omitted.
3. Given either ID exceeds 20 characters (assumed maximum barcode payload length), When barcode generation is attempted, Then the system rejects generation and returns an error code "ERR_BARCODE_PAYLOAD_TOO_LONG" (assumed).

---

**MICROCARE_REQ_002-C: Voucher Slip Rendering with Dual Barcodes**

As a Partner, I need the printed/digital voucher slip to display both the Client barcode and the Partner barcode clearly labeled, so that I can scan either ID independently for accurate redemption and settlement attribution.

Acceptance Criteria:
1. Given a voucher with both barcodes generated, When the voucher slip is rendered, Then the slip displays the Client barcode labeled "Client ID" and the Partner barcode labeled "Partner ID", each with its corresponding human-readable alphanumeric value printed beneath it.
2. Given a voucher with an unassigned Partner ID, When the slip is rendered, Then the Partner barcode section displays the label "Partner ID" with the value "UNASSIGNED00" and both barcode and text remain visible (not hidden or blank).
3. Given the slip is rendered in digital (PDF) format, When viewed at 100% zoom, Then both barcodes are scannable by a standard Code 128 reader at a minimum resolution of 300 DPI (assumed).
notes: N: dictates physical layout (2 portions x 3 tear-off slips 70x50mm); S: ID resolution + barcode gen + PDF rendering

PHIN_REQ_001a: Administrators with system configuration privileges must be able to add custom data fields (of type text, number, date, or single-select list) to existing outbreak management (OM) entities through a no-code, runtime administrative interface, without requiring a software release or developer involvement. A newly added field must be available for data entry, reporting, and data export within 5 minutes (assumed) of being saved. The system must prevent duplicate field names within the same entity and must reject configuration changes that would conflict with reserved system field names.

PHIN_REQ_001b: Administrators with system configuration privileges must be able to define new entity types and new relationship types between entities through the same no-code, runtime administrative interface, specifying for each relationship type its cardinality (one-to-one, one-to-many, or many-to-many) and referential integrity rule (restrict, cascade, or set-null on deletion). The system must prevent deletion of an entity type or relationship type that has existing associated records unless the administrator explicitly selects a migration or cascade-delete option, and must log all such configuration changes with user, timestamp, and before/after values for audit purposes.

PHIN_REQ_001c: All custom fields, entity types, and relationship types created through the administrative configuration interface must be automatically included in standard OM reporting outputs and data export formats (including the system's HL7/FHIR-based exchange format) within 5 minutes (assumed) of creation, with an option for administrators to map custom fields to standard vocabularies (e.g., LOINC, SNOMED CT) for interoperability. Schema changes must be versioned so that existing records created under a prior configuration remain valid and viewable without data loss or corruption after the configuration change.
notes: S: dynamic custom fields + new entity/relationship types + HL7/FHIR export & schema versioning is epic scope

EIRENE_SYS_REQ_003a: The CTCSS tone modulation deviation shall be 0.5 kHz ± 10% (assumed), measured at the transmitter RF output port using a calibrated modulation analyzer, in accordance with the applicable V&V test procedure for CTCSS tone verification (assumed reference: EIRENE_VV_PROC_CTCSS_001).

DII_REQ_002a: The DII Schema Governance Team shall define XSD 1.1 validation constraints (element cardinality, data type, and pattern/regex restrictions) for the DII XML message schema, so that Partner Integration Systems can validate inbound messages without manual schema interpretation. Acceptance criterion: a reference test dataset of 50 valid and 50 invalid XML messages (assumed) shall be validated with 100% correct accept/reject classification against the published XSD.

DII_REQ_002b: The DII Schema Governance Team shall publish the validated XSD schema and an accompanying change log to the organization's existing Schema Registry (assumed pre-existing system) within 1 business day (assumed) of each schema version approval, so that Partner Integration Systems and the Data Exchange Platform team can retrieve the current and prior two schema versions without contacting the DII team directly. Acceptance criterion: a consumer retrieving the schema via the Registry's REST API shall receive the correct schema version and change log entry, verified by an automated integration test.

DII_REQ_002c: The DII Schema Governance Team shall define and document measurable acceptance thresholds for "successful validation" — specifically, zero schema constraint violations and a maximum of 2 seconds (assumed) validation latency per 1 MB message — so that Partner Integration Systems have an objective test oracle for conformance testing before go-live. Negative-path behavior: on validation failure, the validating consumer shall log the specific constraint violated (element path, rule ID, and expected vs. actual value) and reject the message, verified via a negative-path test suite covering at least 10 distinct violation types (assumed).
notes: N: specifies team process/governance workflow; V: internal schema team procedure rather than end-user value; S: XSD + registry + test oracle

text: When a user re-sorts search results on the video search results page (initial sort, column re-sort, or pagination-triggered sort), the system shall render the newly sorted results client-side (assumed) within 0.1 seconds (p95) (assumed), measured from the user's sort-trigger click to the completed re-render, for result sets of up to 1,000 videos (assumed) on a reference environment of a mid-range desktop browser over a broadband connection (assumed), so that the interaction meets Nielsen's instantaneous-response UX heuristic and sustains user engagement with minimal perceived latency.

**QHEADACHE_REQ_002-1 (Functional):**
As a player, I want the product to track and display my active play session time, so that I can maintain screen-time awareness and correlate play duration with headache symptom patterns (assumed rationale, to be confirmed with PO).

The system shall track elapsed play time as follows:
- Timing starts when an active gameplay session begins and stops when the session ends (app closed or user exits to main menu).
- Time accumulates only during active play; it pauses automatically when the app is backgrounded, the device screen locks, or the user manually pauses, and resumes when play resumes.
- Tracking is per-session (resets to zero at the start of each new play session); cumulative totals across sessions are out of scope for this requirement.
- Time is measured and displayed with a precision of whole seconds, formatted as HH:MM:SS.
- If the app crashes or is force-closed, the session timer value is discarded (not persisted) since only active, completed sessions are tracked.
- The timer is unaffected by device timezone or DST changes, as it uses a monotonic elapsed-time clock rather than wall-clock time.

**Out of Scope:** Time limits, parental controls, alerts/notifications, historical charts, multiplayer session aggregation, and cross-session cumulative statistics are not included in this requirement.

**QHEADACHE_REQ_002-2 (Acceptance Criteria):**

Functional scenarios:
1. Given a user starts a new play session, when 90 seconds of active play elapse, then the displayed timer shows "00:01:30" (±1 second accuracy, assumed tolerance).
2. Given an active play session is running, when the user backgrounds the app for 30 seconds and returns, then the displayed timer does not include the 30 seconds of background time and resumes counting from where it paused.
3. Given an active play session, when the user manually pauses and resumes play, then elapsed time during the pause is excluded from the total displayed time.

Non-functional criteria:
- The displayed timer shall refresh at least once per second.
- Timer accuracy shall be within ±1 second (assumed) over a 30-minute continuous play session.
- The timer shall remain accurate and unaffected by OS-level system clock or timezone changes during an active session.

**PHIN_REQ_002a — Manual capture of baseline demographic data for OM case subjects (UI, MVP)**
The Outbreak Management (OM) system shall provide a user interface enabling authorized investigators to manually enter and persist demographic data for persons directly named as case-subjects within an OM investigation record (i.e., individuals formally associated with a confirmed or suspected outbreak case; contacts and providers are out of scope for this requirement). At minimum, the following baseline fields shall be captured, subject to extension per future NNDSS Message Mapping Guide (MMG) updates: name, address, date of birth, gender, phone number, race, ethnicity, and country of citizenship. Subject ID is externally sourced from the organization's Master Person/Patient Index (MPI) system (assumed) and is received, not generated, by OM; if no MPI match exists, the UI shall allow creation of a provisional local Subject ID flagged "unverified" pending MPI reconciliation. Field-level rules: name, date of birth, and Subject ID are mandatory; address, phone number, gender, race, ethnicity, and country of citizenship are optional but must be validated against defined formats when provided (e.g., date of birth as ISO 8601, phone number as E.164). Records with missing optional fields shall save successfully with those fields marked "not collected." This capability traces to NNDSS MMG demographic data elements and supports state health department case reporting and CDC surveillance as the downstream consumers. Acceptance criteria include: mandatory-field enforcement with inline error messages, format validation for date of birth and phone number, successful save with partial optional data, and an audit log entry recording the capturing user and timestamp.

**PHIN_REQ_002b — Controlled vocabulary binding and validation for sensitive demographic fields**
The OM system shall constrain the gender, race, ethnicity, and country of citizenship fields captured under PHIN_REQ_002a to values defined in the PHIN VADS code sets aligned with OMB Statistical Policy Directive 15 (assumed current version), rejecting or flagging any entry not present in the bound vocabulary. The system shall support capture of multiple race values per person per OMB Directive 15 multi-select guidance. Acceptance criteria include: a dropdown or type-ahead control limited to active PHIN VADS code values, rejection of free-text entries for these fields with a user-facing validation message, support for multi-select race entry, and a test case confirming that vocabulary updates (e.g., new PHIN VADS code version) can be applied without a code change, via configuration.

**PHIN_REQ_002c — Programmatic (API/HL7) ingestion of demographic data with Subject ID reconciliation**
The OM system shall expose an API/HL7-based ingestion interface accepting the same baseline demographic field set defined in PHIN_REQ_002a from upstream case management or MDM systems, including the externally sourced Subject ID. This interface depends on, and is blocked until confirmation of, the upstream Subject ID source system's interface specification (named dependency: organizational MPI/MDM system, assumed). Acceptance criteria include: successful ingestion and persistence of a conformant HL7/FHIR message containing all mandatory fields, rejection with a descriptive error code for messages missing mandatory fields or using values outside bound PHIN VADS vocabularies, idempotent handling of duplicate Subject ID submissions, and encryption-in-transit and access-control enforcement (role-based access limited to authorized OM investigator roles) for all demographic data, verified via a dedicated privacy/regulatory compliance test checklist.
notes: I: 002c blocked until upstream MPI/MDM interface spec confirmed; S: manual UI + VADS binding + HL7 API ingestion

**BLITDRAFT_REQ_001-1:** The system shall display, for each of the 8 core functions (assumed: Dashboard, Reports, Settings, Profile, Notifications, Help, Logout, Search), a navigable control (e.g., link, button, or tile) accompanied by a short descriptive label, enabling end-users to discover and access these functions without prior training.

**BLITDRAFT_REQ_001-2:** For each function control, the system shall determine availability based on the end-user's assigned role. Controls for functions the user is not authorized to use shall be rendered in a visibly disabled state with an explanatory tooltip stating "You do not have permission to access this function" (assumed). Controls for authorized functions shall, upon selection, navigate the user to the corresponding function screen within 2 seconds (assumed).

**BLITDRAFT_REQ_001-3:** All function controls and their descriptive labels shall comply with WCAG 2.1 Level AA accessibility guidelines (assumed), including providing accessible names for screen readers. If a selected function's target screen fails to load within 5 seconds (assumed), the system shall display the message "This function is temporarily unavailable, please try again later" (assumed) instead of a broken or blank screen.

THEMAS_REQ_001a: The THEMAS system shall accept temperature readings in the range of -40°C to 125°C (assumed), inclusive of both boundary values, as valid input for processing.

THEMAS_REQ_001b: The THEMAS system shall detect any temperature reading that is outside the range of -40°C to 125°C (assumed) or that is malformed (e.g., NaN, null, or non-numeric input) within 1 second (assumed) of receipt.

THEMAS_REQ_001c: Upon detecting an out-of-range or malformed temperature reading as defined in THEMAS_REQ_001b, the THEMAS system shall discard the invalid reading, retain the last known valid temperature value for control purposes, and generate an alarm notification to the operator interface within 2 seconds (assumed) of detection.

EIRENE_FUN_REQ_001: Mobile terminals shall support operation in the Railways GSM (R-GSM) band, with uplink 876–880 MHz and downlink 921–925 MHz, and in the public GSM bands (E-GSM/P-GSM), with uplink 880–915 MHz and downlink 925–960 MHz, in accordance with ECC Decision (02)05 and ETSI EN 301 515. This requirement applies to all cab radio and handheld terminal classes defined for EIRENE-compliant mobile equipment (assumed). Terminals shall be capable of selecting and camping on either band individually, based on network availability and configured priority, but are not required to transmit or receive on both bands simultaneously. Compliance shall be verified through conformance testing per the EN 301 515 test specification, with acceptance criteria including successful RF lock within 2 seconds (assumed) on each band and call setup success rate of at least 99% (assumed) across 100 consecutive attempts per band under nominal signal conditions.

1. When a peering node in the compute-resource pool (database connections, message-queue workers, and peering network links) (assumed) transitions to a Failed state — defined as three consecutive missed health-check responses within 30 seconds (assumed) — the monitoring service shall send a failure alert to the on-call SRE team via PagerDuty within 30 seconds (assumed) of detection, to enable faster incident response and reduced Mean Time To Recovery (MTTR).

2. Each failure alert shall contain, at minimum: the resource identifier, resource category, failure timestamp, and last-known-good timestamp, formatted as a structured JSON payload (assumed), so that on-call SRE staff can triage without consulting additional systems.

3. If the monitoring service itself fails to deliver an alert within 60 seconds (assumed) of detecting a resource failure, it shall escalate via a secondary channel — email to the SRE distribution list (assumed) — and log the delivery failure, so that silent failures of the reporting mechanism itself are detectable and auditable.

EIRENE_FUN_REQ_002 (compliance-traceability anchor, preserved verbatim): A visual and audible indication shall be given when the remaining capacity of the battery is such as to enable only 10 minutes of full duplex call time.

EIRENE_FUN_REQ_002a (derives-from EIRENE_FUN_REQ_002 — capacity-to-call-time estimation): The device shall estimate remaining full-duplex call time from the battery's measured remaining capacity using a discharge model that accounts for cell chemistry and aging, duty cycle (continuous full-duplex transmit/receive), and operating temperature range of -20°C to +55°C (assumed). The estimation shall be accurate to within ±1 minute (assumed) of actual remaining full-duplex call time when verified against a bench test with simulated battery discharge profiles covering the full specified temperature and aging range. The estimation function shall update at least once every 30 seconds (assumed) during an active call.

EIRENE_FUN_REQ_002b (derives-from EIRENE_FUN_REQ_002a — dual-modality low-battery alert): When the estimated remaining full-duplex call time computed per EIRENE_FUN_REQ_002a falls to 10 minutes or less, the device shall trigger a combined visual and audible indication. The indication shall be triggered once within a tolerance band of 10 minutes ±30 seconds (assumed) and shall not re-trigger or flap if estimated call time fluctuates within that band (hysteresis of 1 minute, assumed). The visual indication shall remain active and perceptible under cab ambient light levels up to 10,000 lux (assumed) until the call ends or the device is powered off. The audible indication shall be a repeating tone at a minimum of 75 dB(A) (assumed) at 1 meter, audible above a cab noise floor of up to 65 dB(A) (assumed), repeating at least once every 30 seconds (assumed) until acknowledged by the user or the call ends. Conformance shall be verified by bench test using simulated battery discharge to produce the trigger condition, with measurement of visual perceptibility and audible sound pressure level against the stated thresholds.
notes: S: combines battery discharge physics model + dual-modality hardware alert + hysteresis

SWPROJ_REQ_007a: The system shall display a tiered location-permission consent flow (iOS "When In Use" / "Always Allow" and Android "Allow only while using the app" / "Allow all the time") before enabling any background location tracking, so that users can grant delivery-ETA tracking ("Always Allow"/"Allow all the time") with informed consent, consistent with Apple App Store Review Guideline §5.1.1 and Google Play's location permissions policy. Acceptance criteria: the system must correctly record and branch on each of the four permission states (granted-when-in-use, granted-always, denied, not-yet-determined) and re-prompt according to platform-specific rules (max 1 re-prompt per session, assumed).

SWPROJ_REQ_007b: When a user has granted "Always Allow" (iOS) or "Allow all the time" (Android) permission, the system shall continuously acquire device location while the app is backgrounded or suspended (not force-terminated), using Core Location (iOS) or the Fused Location Provider (Android), so that real-time delivery ETA can be computed and displayed to the recipient. The service shall report location updates at a minimum interval of 60 seconds (assumed) or 50 meters of displacement (assumed), whichever occurs first, and shall not exceed 3% additional battery drain per hour of active tracking (assumed), measured on a reference device (iPhone 12 / Pixel 6, assumed) under standard conditions.

SWPROJ_REQ_007c: The system shall detect and respond to permission revocation or app termination during an active background-tracking session within 5 seconds (assumed) by halting location acquisition, discarding any unflushed location payloads larger than 1 KB (assumed) that have not yet been transmitted, and notifying the delivery-tracking backend that live ETA updates are no longer available, so that downstream consumers (e.g., the recipient-facing ETA screen) can fall back to a static estimate without leaking stale or unauthorized location data.
notes: S: tiered OS consent flow + continuous background GPS + revocation abort handling

PEPPOL_APPROVED_REQ_001a: The data model MUST define a standard, machine-readable representation of the exclusion criteria set out in Article 45 of Directive 2004/18/EC (e.g., convictions, professional misconduct, non-payment of taxes/social security), expressed as a closed baseline schema that national implementations MAY extend with additive, clearly flagged national criteria elements without breaking baseline conformance (assumed additive-extensible tier). This requirement covers the data model only; transport and exchange mechanics (e.g., AS2, PEPPOL BIS envelopes) are explicitly out of scope and governed separately. It depends on, and MUST be aligned with, the pre-existing ESPD schema and CEN/BII core component library as the authoritative base components (assumed dependency sequencing: CEN/BII core components finalized first, ESPD schema second, this schema third). Acceptance is measured by: (1) a published XSD/JSON schema with one conformance test suite containing at least 10 sample instance documents (assumed) covering each exclusion ground and at least 2 national-derogation examples, validated with zero errors; (2) at least 90% (assumed) of a sample of contracting authorities' exclusion data being consumable without custom mapping, verified via pilot testing.

PEPPOL_APPROVED_REQ_001b: The data model MUST define a standard, machine-readable representation of the selection criteria set out in Articles 46-50 of Directive 2004/18/EC, covering professional registration (Art. 46), economic/financial standing (Art. 47), technical/professional capacity (Art. 48), quality assurance standards (Art. 49), and environmental management standards (Art. 50), as five discrete, independently versionable sub-schemas within one additive-extensible baseline schema (assumed conformance tier), allowing member states to layer additional criteria without invalidating baseline documents. This requirement covers the data model only; transport and exchange mechanics are out of scope. It depends on, and MUST reuse, the pre-existing ESPD schema data elements and CEN/BII core components as defined for exclusion criteria in a companion exclusion-criteria data model requirement. Acceptance is measured by: (1) a published schema with a conformance test suite containing at least 15 sample instance documents (assumed), covering at least 2 examples per sub-schema plus 1 national-derogation example per sub-schema, validated with zero errors; (2) a measured 25% reduction (assumed) in manual cross-border ESPD reconciliation effort, confirmed via a before/after pilot with at least 3 contracting authorities (assumed).

PEPPOL_APPROVED_REQ_001c: Before implementation of PEPPOL_APPROVED_REQ_001a and PEPPOL_APPROVED_REQ_001b, the Product Owner and legal SME MUST jointly confirm, as a single gating decision, whether this schema work is (i) a historical/audit artifact that remains fixed to Directive 2004/18/EC literal text, or (ii) a live re-groom requiring a mapped update to the equivalent provisions of Directive 2014/24/EU (assumed successor legal basis), and MUST record this decision, together with the chosen conformance tier (closed vs. additive-extensible schema) and the definitive meaning of "common criteria" (harmonized-only vocabulary vs. baseline-plus-extension model), in a single approved decision record before any child schema is finalized. This decision record itself constitutes the test oracle for all conformance testing of PEPPOL_APPROVED_REQ_001a and PEPPOL_APPROVED_REQ_001b and MUST be completed within 10 business days (assumed) of this requirement's approval.
notes: I: depends on finalizing CEN/BII, ESPD schema, and 001c PO/legal gating decision; S: Art 45 + Art 46-50 schemas

**SWPROJ_REQ_006**: When an audio file fails to load due to one of the following v1-supported failure causes: unsupported format, file corruption, or missing file (assumed), the system shall display a user-facing error message that includes: (1) a plain-language description of the cause (e.g., "This file format is not supported," "The file could not be found," or "This file appears to be damaged"), and (2) a suggested next action (e.g., "Try a different file" or "Check the file path and try again"). The message shall not display raw error codes, exception names, or stack traces.

**SWPROJ_REQ_006a**: The error message shall be verifiable using the following deterministic test fixtures: a file with an unsupported extension/codec (e.g., a renamed .txt file or an unsupported codec sample), a corrupted audio file (e.g., a truncated .mp3 with invalid headers), and a reference to a non-existent file path. For each fixture, the displayed message shall match the corresponding cause-specific text defined in SWPROJ_REQ_006, with no raw error codes or jargon present.

EIRENE_SYS_REQ_001a: The system shall detect non-successful establishment of a Railway emergency call if establishment has not completed within 2 seconds (±200 ms tolerance) (assumed), measured from the timestamp of the user's call-initiation action (timer start) to the timestamp of either a confirmed call-established event or an explicit failure event (timer stop). Non-successful establishment shall include, at minimum, the following enumerated failure modes: (a) timeout with no network response, (b) explicit call rejection by the network, (c) unavailable bearer/no coverage, and (d) barred service access (per EIRENE FRS/SRS call-control failure taxonomy, Section 7.4 (assumed)). This 2-second threshold is a fixed safety-related parameter traceable to EIRENE SRS clause 13.4.2.1 (assumed) and shall not be altered without hazard log review (Hazard Log ID HL-EC-014 (assumed)).

EIRENE_SYS_REQ_001b: Upon detection of a non-successful establishment event as defined in EIRENE_SYS_REQ_001a, the system shall provide the user with a visual and audible indication (assumed modality, per EIRENE SRS clause 13.4.2.3 (assumed)) within 500 ms (assumed) of the failure event. The indication shall display the specific failure mode (timeout, rejection, no bearer, or barred) using distinct, predefined status codes or icons, and shall persist on the user interface until acknowledged by the user or until a new call-establishment attempt is initiated, whichever occurs first.

EIRENE_SYS_REQ_001c: During the establishment attempt, prior to a non-successful or successful outcome, the system shall provide the user with a continuous "in-progress" indication distinguishable from both the success and failure indications. Upon successful establishment, the system shall provide a distinct success indication within 500 ms (assumed) of the confirmed call-established event. If retry or escalation procedures are triggered after a non-successful attempt, each retry shall restart the 2-second detection timer independently (per-attempt basis), and the status indication shall update to reflect the current attempt's state.

**SWPROJ_REQ_003-A (Reachability check and error display):**
The system shall evaluate the reachability of each generated location at generation-time, immediately after the location coordinates are produced and before they are presented to the user, by performing coordinate bounds-checking and obstacle/collision detection against the current navigation mesh (assumed). If this check determines the location is unreachable (i.e., no valid path exists between the user's current position and the generated coordinates), the system shall display the error message "Selected location is unreachable. Please generate a new location." within 1 second (assumed) of the check completing, and shall not allow the unreachable location to be selected or navigated to.

*Acceptance Criteria:*
- Given a location has just been generated, When the reachability check determines no valid path exists to the location, Then the system displays the message "Selected location is unreachable. Please generate a new location." within 1 second (assumed), and the location remains unselectable.

**SWPROJ_REQ_003-B (No error for reachable locations):**
The system shall not display any error message when the generation-time reachability check determines that a valid path exists between the user's current position and the generated location.

*Acceptance Criteria:*
- Given a location has just been generated, When the reachability check determines a valid path exists to the location, Then no error message is displayed and the location is presented to the user as selectable.

GAMMA_J_REQ_002a: When a user adds a product to the shopping cart, the system shall update the in-memory cart/session state (independent of downstream inventory availability checks, pricing recalculation, or persistent database writes, which are handled by separate operations) and shall return a success acknowledgment to the client.

GAMMA_J_REQ_002b: The server-side processing time for the add-to-cart operation (measured from receipt of the add-to-cart request at the application server to generation of the response, excluding network transit time) shall be less than or equal to 200ms (assumed) at the 95th percentile (p95), under a sustained load of 500 concurrent users (assumed), as verified through automated performance/load testing (e.g., JMeter or equivalent) in a staging environment configured to mirror production. This target supports the system's scalability requirements under peak traffic and contributes to reducing cart-abandonment rates caused by perceptible delay.

**PEERING_REQ_002a — Reject malformed or injection-pattern requests at the gateway**
Given a peering request payload received at the gateway, when the payload fails schema validation (e.g., contains SQL injection patterns such as `' OR '1'='1`, oversized fields exceeding 8 KB (assumed), or invalid protocol framing), then the gateway shall reject the request with HTTP 400 (Bad Request) within 200 ms (assumed), log the rejection with request source IP, timestamp, and matched rule ID, and achieve a false-positive rate below 0.1% (assumed) and false-negative rate below 1% (assumed) when evaluated against a labeled benign/malicious traffic corpus of at least 10,000 samples (assumed).

**PEERING_REQ_002b — Reject requests exceeding rate limits**
Given a peering client identified by API key or IP address, when the client exceeds 100 requests per minute (assumed), then the system shall reject subsequent requests with HTTP 429 (Too Many Requests) including a `Retry-After` header, log the event with client identifier, timestamp, and current request count, and ensure legitimate clients below the threshold experience no more than 0.5% (assumed) false rejections during load testing.

**PEERING_REQ_002c — Reject duplicate or replayed session requests**
Given a peering session request containing a unique session token, when a request with an already-used or expired token (older than 5 minutes, assumed) is received, then the system shall reject it with HTTP 409 (Conflict), log the duplicate/replay attempt with token ID, originating IP, and timestamp, and correctly identify at least 99% (assumed) of replayed tokens in a test corpus of 1,000 duplicate-session attempts while rejecting no more than 0.1% (assumed) of legitimate retries.
notes: S: bundles SQLi/payload validation + rate limiting (HTTP 429) + replay token detection (HTTP 409)

**SWPROJ_REQ_008a**
As a traveler using the mobile app, I want to receive a push notification when I arrive at my destination, so that I have immediate confirmation that navigation is complete and I can safely stop following directions.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- **Platform scope:** iOS and Android native apps only (assumed); web push excluded from this requirement.
- **Arrival detection:** The system shall consider the destination "reached" when the user's device-reported GPS location is within a 50-meter radius (assumed) of the destination coordinate, with a GPS horizontal accuracy of 20 meters or better (assumed).
- **Given** the user has an active route with a single destination point and has granted location permissions (foreground or background),
  **When** the device's GPS location enters the 50-meter arrival geofence,
  **Then** the system shall trigger exactly one push notification within 5 seconds (assumed) of geofence entry, regardless of whether the app is foregrounded, backgrounded, or terminated.
- **Given** the user has already received an arrival notification for the current route,
  **When** the device location fluctuates in and out of the geofence radius (GPS drift),
  **Then** the system shall suppress duplicate notifications for that route instance.
- **Given** the user has denied location permissions,
  **When** the destination would otherwise be reached,
  **Then** no push notification shall be sent, and the app shall display an in-app banner (assumed) indicating that arrival detection is unavailable due to permission settings.
- **Given** the device is offline (no network connectivity) at the moment of geofence entry,
  **When** connectivity is restored within 10 minutes (assumed),
  **Then** the system shall deliver the arrival notification retroactively; if connectivity is not restored within that window, the notification shall be discarded.

**SWPROJ_REQ_008b**
As a dispatcher monitoring multiple active deliveries or trips, I want to receive a push notification when a traveler under my supervision reaches their destination, so that I can confirm delivery or trip completion without manually checking each traveler's status.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- **Given** a dispatcher is subscribed to a traveler's trip,
  **When** the traveler's device triggers an arrival event per the 50-meter geofence rule (assumed),
  **Then** the dispatcher's app shall receive a push notification within 10 seconds (assumed) of the traveler's arrival notification being generated.
- Multi-stop routes (if applicable) are out of scope for this requirement and will be addressed in a separate requirement once the destination model (single-point vs. multi-stop) is confirmed via technical spike (assumed).
notes: S: traveler background geofence push + offline retroactive delivery + dispatcher multi-trip notification

**SWPROJ_REQ_005-A — Proximity/Geofence Detection**
Depends on: SWPROJ_REQ_TARGETLOC-CRUD (target location data management), SWPROJ_REQ_LOCPERM (location permission handling).
Rationale: Enables location-aware guidance for mobile app users (assumed persona: field visitors using a walking-tour app) by notifying the system when they approach a point of interest, so relevant audio content can be delivered without manual interaction.
The system shall continuously monitor the user's GPS position while the mobile app (iOS and Android, assumed) is in foreground or background state and detect when the user's position enters a circular geofence of 30 meters radius (straight-line distance, assumed) around any active target location, using a positioning accuracy tolerance of ±10 meters (assumed) with GPS as primary source and network-based location as fallback when GPS signal is unavailable. The system shall raise a "zone entry" event within 3 seconds (assumed) of the user's position satisfying the geofence condition. To prevent repeated triggering while the user lingers or moves in and out of the boundary, the system shall apply a debounce period of 60 seconds (assumed) before a re-entry into the same zone can raise a new event. If location permissions are denied or revoked, the system shall suspend geofence monitoring and log a "monitoring suspended" status without crashing or raising false events.

**SWPROJ_REQ_005-B — Voice Playback Trigger**
Depends on: SWPROJ_REQ_005-A (zone entry event), SWPROJ_REQ_AUDIOASSET-MGMT (audio asset management and association with target locations).
Rationale: Ensures users receive timely, relevant audio information at points of interest, improving engagement without requiring manual playback actions.
Upon receiving a "zone entry" event from the proximity detection subsystem, the system shall automatically begin playback of the audio asset associated with that target location within 2 seconds (assumed) of event receipt, provided no other triggered playback is currently active. If playback is already in progress when a new zone entry event occurs, the system shall queue the new audio asset and play it after the current playback completes (assumed behavior), rather than interrupting or overlapping audio. If a user's position simultaneously satisfies the entry condition for multiple overlapping target zones, the system shall trigger playback for the zone whose center is closest to the user's current position and queue the remaining zone's audio per the above queuing rule.
notes: I: depends on external TARGETLOC-CRUD, LOCPERM, and AUDIOASSET-MGMT reqs; S: GPS geofencing + audio playback queue

**SWPROJ_REQ_001 (Core coordinate generation):**
The system shall generate a random geographic coordinate (latitude/longitude in WGS84, decimal degrees, precision to 6 decimal places) located within an annulus around the user's current location, with an inner radius of 2 km and outer radius of 5 km (assumed configurable system parameters, defaulting to 2 km and 5 km respectively). The coordinate shall be drawn using an area-uniform random distribution (equal probability per unit area across the annulus) rather than uniform-radius sampling, to prevent clustering near the inner boundary. This requirement is scoped strictly to the coordinate-generation algorithm; it excludes location-permission handling, real-world validity filtering (e.g., land/water or restricted-zone checks), and persistence/display of the generated coordinate, which shall be addressed as separate requirements. The function shall return a generated coordinate within 100 ms (assumed) per request under typical load.

**SWPROJ_REQ_001a (Acceptance criteria / testability):**
Given a fixed user location, a sample of 1,000 generated coordinates (assumed sample size) shall each have a haversine distance to the user location that is ≥2.000 km and ≤5.000 km inclusive, allowing a rounding tolerance of ±1 meter. The sample distribution shall pass a chi-square goodness-of-fit test against the expected area-uniform distribution at a 95% confidence level (assumed). The coordinate-generation function shall accept an optional random seed parameter to enable deterministic, repeatable output for automated test execution.

**SWPROJ_REQ_001b (Configurability):**
The 2 km and 5 km radius values shall be exposed as configurable parameters (not hard-coded constants), allowing stakeholders to adjust the annulus bounds without code changes; the default values of 2 km and 5 km (assumed) shall apply unless overridden via configuration.

SWPROJ_REQ_011a: The system shall allow only the authenticated owner of a user profile to read and write files under the Firebase Storage path `/users/{userId}/profile/`, and shall deny all other authenticated or anonymous users. Given a signed-in user with UID "A", when user "A" uploads or downloads a file at `/users/A/profile/avatar.jpg`, then the operation shall succeed with a 200 status. Given a signed-in user with UID "B" attempts to read or write a file at `/users/A/profile/`, then the operation shall be denied with a 403 status and the attempt shall be logged (assumed) to Firebase Storage access logs.

SWPROJ_REQ_011b: The system shall allow members of a shared project (identified by membership in the project's `members` list in Firestore) to read and write files under `/projects/{projectId}/documents/`, and shall deny access to non-members. Given a user listed in the `members` array of project "P123", when that user uploads or downloads a file at `/projects/P123/documents/report.pdf`, then the operation shall succeed with a 200 status. Given a user not listed as a member of project "P123", when that user attempts to read or write a file at `/projects/P123/documents/`, then the operation shall be denied with a 403 status.

SWPROJ_REQ_011c: The system shall restrict read, write, and delete operations on files under `/admin/` to users whose custom claim includes `role: "admin"`, and shall deny these operations to all other users, including authenticated non-admin users. Given a user with the custom claim `role: "admin"`, when that user performs a read, write, or delete operation on any file under `/admin/`, then the operation shall succeed with a 200 status. Given a user without the `admin` role, when that user attempts any operation under `/admin/`, then the operation shall be denied with a 403 status within 2 seconds (assumed) and the denial shall be recorded in the security audit log.
notes: S: covers 3 separate RBAC scopes (user profile, shared project docs, and admin paths)

QHEADACHE_REQ_001a: Within a single editing session of the document editor module (assumed scope), the user must be able to undo their most recent discrete action, where a "discrete action" is defined as one atomic, user-initiated change (e.g., text insertion/deletion, formatting change, object move) tracked as a single entry in the undo history (assumed definition). Each undo must fully reverse the state change caused by that action, verified by comparing document state before the action and after the undo.

QHEADACHE_REQ_001b: After performing one or more undo operations, the user must be able to redo the most recently undone action(s), restoring the document to the exact state prior to the undo. If the user performs any new discrete action after an undo (and before a redo), the redo stack must be invalidated and cleared, discarding all previously undone actions beyond that point.

QHEADACHE_REQ_001c: The undo/redo history depth target is an open parameter to be negotiated with the product owner and validated against user research or support data (e.g., analysis of undo-related support tickets) rather than fixed in advance. As a starting point for discussion, the system should support a history depth of 100 actions per session (assumed, subject to negotiation), retained in memory only (not persisted across sessions, assumed) for the editing session's duration. When the depth limit is reached, the oldest action in the history must be evicted on a first-in-first-out basis to make room for the newest action, without degrading undo/redo responsiveness: each undo or redo operation must complete within 200 milliseconds (assumed) under typical document sizes, and no data corruption or partial-state application may occur during eviction or during undo/redo execution.

SWPROJ_REQ_002-A: The system shall display an interactive map showing up to 100 target points (assumed), defined as delivery destinations (assumed), on the mobile platform (assumed), so that field users can identify and navigate to assigned delivery locations.
Acceptance criteria:
- Given the user opens the map screen, when target point data is available, then all target points within the current map viewport are rendered within 2 seconds (assumed) of screen load.
- Given no target points exist for the user, when the map loads, then the system displays an empty-state message "No target points assigned" instead of a blank map.
- Given target point data fails to load, when the map screen opens, then the system displays an error message and offers a retry option.

SWPROJ_REQ_002-B: The system shall overlay the user's real-time position on the map so that field users can monitor their current location relative to target points for navigation purposes.
Acceptance criteria:
- Given the user has granted foreground location permission, when the user's GPS position updates, then the map marker reflects the new position within 5 seconds (assumed) with accuracy of ±10 meters (assumed).
- Given the user has not granted location permission, when the map loads, then the system prompts the user with a permission request explaining the purpose of location use.
- Given the user denies or revokes location permission, when the map is displayed, then the system shows a persistent notice "Location unavailable" and hides the position marker instead of showing a stale or default location.
- Given GPS signal is lost after being acquired, when no position update is received for 30 seconds (assumed), then the system displays a "Signal lost" indicator on the map.

SWPROJ_REQ_002-C: The system shall provide interactive map controls (pinch-to-zoom, drag-to-pan, and tap-to-select a target point) so that field users can efficiently explore the map and inspect target point details without delay.
Acceptance criteria:
- Given the user performs a pinch-to-zoom or drag-to-pan gesture, when the gesture is completed, then the map view updates with a perceived lag of less than 200 milliseconds (assumed).
- Given the user taps a target point marker, when the tap is registered, then the system displays the target point's name and coordinates within 500 milliseconds (assumed).
- Given the user taps an area of the map with no target point, when the tap is registered, then no detail panel is shown and the map remains in its current state.
notes: S: map target rendering + live GPS overlay + interactive gestures/detail panel

CCTNS_REQ_001a: As a System Administrator, I want to activate or deactivate the audit trail subsystem, so that audit logging can be controlled in compliance with the system's evidence integrity and chain-of-custody policy (assumed: CCTNS Information Security and Evidence Management Policy). The System shall allow an Administrator with the "Security Administrator" role to toggle the audit trail subsystem to "Active" or "Inactive" via a dedicated administrative control. Acceptance criteria: (1) Given the subsystem is "Inactive", when an Administrator sets it to "Active", then the System shall begin capturing events within 2 seconds (assumed) and record the activation action itself as an audit event. (2) Given the subsystem is "Active", when an Administrator attempts to deactivate it, then the System shall require a secondary approval (assumed: four-eyes principle) and log the deactivation request, approver identity, and timestamp. (3) If deactivation is attempted while a transaction is in progress, the System shall complete audit capture for that transaction before applying the deactivation (fail-closed behavior).

CCTNS_REQ_002b: As a Compliance/System Auditor, I want the System to automatically capture a defined set of security-relevant and case-relevant events, so that a complete, non-repudiable activity record exists to support investigations and regulatory audits (assumed linkage: CCTNS Evidence Integrity and Chain-of-Custody Mandate). While the audit trail subsystem is "Active", the System shall automatically capture, without manual intervention, the following event types (assumed enumerable taxonomy): user login/logout, user creation/modification/deactivation, case record create/update/delete, evidence record create/update/delete, workflow status transitions, and permission/role changes. For each captured event, the System shall record: event timestamp (UTC, millisecond precision), actor user ID, actor role, action type, affected entity ID and type, before-state and after-state values (where applicable), source IP/terminal ID, and outcome (success/failure). Acceptance criteria: (1) Given the subsystem is "Active", when any listed event occurs, then a corresponding audit record with all mandatory fields shall be created within 1 second (assumed) of the event. (2) Given two events occur concurrently on the same entity, when both are processed, then both shall be recorded as distinct, correctly sequenced audit entries with no data loss. (3) Given the System crashes mid-event, when it recovers, then any incomplete audit record shall be flagged as "incomplete" rather than silently discarded.

CCTNS_REQ_003c: As a Compliance/System Auditor, I want captured audit data to be stored durably, tamper-evident, access-controlled, and retained per policy, so that the audit trail remains legally defensible and available for inspection (assumed linkage: CCTNS Records Retention Policy, 7-year minimum retention for law-enforcement audit data). The System shall persist each audit record to a write-once storage medium or equivalent append-only log store, apply a cryptographic hash chain (assumed: SHA-256) across sequential records to enable tamper detection, and retain all audit records for a minimum of 7 years (assumed) before archival. Access to view or export audit logs shall be restricted to users holding the "Compliance Auditor" or "Security Administrator" role, and every view/export action shall itself generate an audit record. Acceptance criteria: (1) Given an audit record has been persisted, when any field of that record is altered outside the designated audit process, then the next integrity check shall detect and flag the tamper event. (2) Given a user without the required role attempts to access audit logs, when the access request is made, then the System shall deny access and log the denied attempt. (3) Given the retention period has not elapsed, when a deletion request for audit data is submitted, then the System shall reject the request and log the rejected attempt.
notes: S: audit toggle with four-eyes approval + 10-event auto-capture + 7-year SHA-256 tamper-evident store
